turns.content: Let S_2(m) be the number of 1s in the binary expansion of m. Compute S_2(2020) and prove that 2020 cannot be written as a sum of fewer than S_2(2020) powers of two.
Denote the binary digit sum obtained above by s and use it in the payoff bounds.

Analyze A's strategy of repeatedly choosing two equal nonzero entries. Show that all nonzero entries remain powers of two, that the strategy continues until termination, and that A secures at least s cookies.

Call a sign assignment balanced when sum epsilon_i x_i=0, and a position good when its number of balanced assignments is not divisible by 2^(s+1). Prove the initial position is good using the 2-adic valuation of C(2020,1010).
After A removes any two entries, prove B can preserve goodness without assuming the previous position was good.
Analyze both terminal conditions and prove that a terminal good position has at most s entries.
Check that a dominating entry gives no balanced assignments, whereas k zeros give 2^k balanced assignments.
Combine A's lower bound and B's good-position strategy to determine the optimal payoff.
